svg.aria-label: A cited commit is resolved against the repository, and a citation that resolves to nothing is refused before the row is written.
svg.text: Two citations of identical shape, and the one instrument that separates them
cited in the manifest as a landed commit
7892cb69 6b2fbb52ac9b3e2ded0f5a5a26a3b2d1
40 hex characters · right prefix · no object behind it
the commit the run actually wrote
same length, same eight-character prefix
the citation check
ask the store about the value as cited, never about its form
git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options <value>^{commit}
a shape check cannot answer this: both values pass it
a length check is worse than useless — it manufactured a
fabrication once, because compliance meant guessing
so the check reads resolution, and nothing else
what promotion does with the answer
resolves
the row records the canonical object id, so an honest
abbreviation or a tag stays useful
commits: [canonical id]
resolves to nothing
refused before the row is written, naming the citation
the run id and the repository that was asked
no row · the run is left to fix
a manifest that declares no commit — commits: none (…) — cites no identifier, so no store is asked and nothing is refused
the refusal carries the citation and the run id, so a fabricated sha is read as a defect rather than filed as evidence
